rationale:
Quota: 1 long, 3 Shorts, 0 carousels. Everything sits inside the GLP-1 focus and is tirzepatide-first.

Long-form: 3 of the last 7 long videos were search-demand formats (first month 11-13, pen how-to 11-11, Foundayo what-to-expect 11-11), so today can be a broad Lane A topic. The breadth rule says broad questions beat narrow single-symptom long videos (2,980 vs 231 min), so I took the playbook's next broad item, "foods that ease side effects". Nausea, diarrhoea, constipation and heartburn become chapters instead of separate videos. The body rests on settled sources: the Zepbound label, the 2025 joint nutrition advisory and NHS pages. It is not a single-trial deep dive, and the holiday-meal searches (Nov 20–28) give it an evergreen run-up.

Skipped long options:
- Keeping results after stopping repeats the 11-04 Stopping video's SURMOUNT-4 and habits angle within 30 days.
- Months 1–6 overlaps "How Long" (10-20) and First Month (11-13).
- The NAION label change was covered by a Short on 11-10 and is still peaking.
- REDEFINE 4 has no fresh randomized data yet, so it stays a watch item.

Shorts: 2 of the 3 are felt symptoms or practical moments.
- S1 is a pen moment (a drop after the shot). It's off the gut so the day doesn't stack three digestive pieces, and it's in our winning injection/pen Short category.
- S2 is the 13:00 lead. "Tirzepatide not working?" uses the Nature GLP1R-variant paper as evidence inside the Short, not as its topic. It's emerging with low competition.
- S3 is a spin-off of L1 (greasy food), which feeds the long video.

The Exp F lines still apply to S1 (08:00) and S2 (13:00) until the test closes on 11-17. Rejected or caution radar items (the psychiatric case reports, alcohol, pregnancy) were left out of today's slate.

pieces.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound) and food: which eating habits and food choices may ease the common stomach side effects (nausea, diarrhoea, constipation, heartburn and burping), why slower stomach emptying makes meal size, fat and pace matter, and when symptoms mean calling a prescriber
pieces.angle:
Broad Lane A long video (log 'lane: A'; publisher adds it to 'Life on Tirzepatide'). Runs 9–11 min at 14:00 ET. Evergreen, with no date or holiday words.

Opening:
- Sentence 1 names tirzepatide and the viewer's question, then gives a short answer by 15 s: smaller meals, eating slowly, stopping at comfortably full and going easier on greasy food are the habits experts suggest most often.
- Next comes a 'you' scenario: a rich dinner sits like a brick.
- At 15–30 s, give the second concrete payoff: the label's pooled nausea rate per dose vs placebo, plus the label's wording that GI effects happened mostly during dose escalation and decreased over time. Never shorten that timing to 'first weeks'.

Chapters, each named as a searched question:
1. Why does food feel different on tirzepatide? Use the label's delayed-gastric-emptying wording.
2. What to eat when you're nauseous. Credit only what the 2025 ACLM/ASN/OMA/TOS advisory says ('avoiding fatty or high fiber foods during the first few days of treatment', at exactly that scope; smaller, more frequent meals). Bland options and eating slowly are untagged tips.
3. Foods for diarrhoea, and fluids. Sip fluids unless you've been told to limit them. Use the label's dehydration and kidney wording, and tag the NHS dehydration signs to NHS.
4. Foods for constipation. Build fibre up gradually with fluids, and explain why that doesn't conflict with the 'first few days' advice.
5. Heartburn and burping. NHS reflux advice goes in only as NHS prints it. 'Sulfur burps' is called a commonly described symptom, with no cause given.
6. Protein when appetite is low. Include the kidney caveat.
7. When to call. Severe stomach pain that won't go away, with or without vomiting, means stop and call your healthcare provider right away. Signs of dehydration or vomiting you can't keep up with means contact your prescriber. Then: 'For anything that isn't one of those emergency signs, don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own.'

Rules:
- All habits are 'recommended', never 'proven on tirzepatide'.
- Give label rates with both arms and name the pooled-trial population. Mounjaro rates only if labelled as type 2 diabetes trials.
- Add the low-blood-sugar caveat for people on insulin or a sulfonylurea.
- No foods called 'bad', no calorie talk, no products, doses or titration.
- Land a payoff before the ~70 s chapter change. Re-hook every 45–75 s. One subscribe ask, after the chapter 2–4 payoff. Start the end ask at about 85%.
- Include 'Not personal advice' and the full prescriber line.
- End with: 'There's a video I'd watch next, linked in the description.'
- Publisher: line-1 ▶ Watch next link to Side Effects.
- Thumbnail: 4 words or fewer that keep the gap, e.g. 'Which Foods Help?', with one calm, labelled tummy character. No body imagery.
pieces.target_keyword: foods to eat on mounjaro for nausea
pieces.why: #3 in the playbook's broad Lane A queue. Broad side-effect questions earn the most (Side Effects has 1,064 min), the narrow-symptom rule turns nausea, constipation, diarrhoea and heartburn into chapters, and holiday-meal searches spike Nov 20–28.

pieces.topic: A drop of liquid or blood at the injection spot after a tirzepatide pen shot: what the Instructions for Use say it means, and when to call
pieces.angle:
08:00 'Is this normal?' practical-moment Short, tight arm.
- Sentence 1 (14 words or fewer): 'Drop of liquid or blood after your tirzepatide shot? Here's what the pen guide says.'
- By 6 s, give the Instructions for Use's own explanation of a drop of medicine or blood at the site. Quote it only if the IFU text loads; otherwise paraphrase without quotes.
- Scope: the US single-dose pen. KwikPens and vials have different steps, so check the leaflet in your box or ask a pharmacist.
- New fact: the label's injection-site reaction rates, 6–8% by dose vs about 2% on placebo.
- Untagged red flags: spreading redness, warmth, pus or fever means call your prescriber. In label wording: swelling of the face, lips or throat, or trouble breathing, means your local emergency number.
- Then the scoped don't-stop line, the Exp F line second to last, 'Not personal advice', the prescriber line and the closing line.
- No doses, missed-dose or technique coaching beyond the IFU.
- Post note: the related-video target is the pen how-to long video (11-11).

pieces.topic: Tirzepatide not working as well for you as for others? Why weight-loss responses differ: the SURMOUNT-1 spread, lower average loss with type 2 diabetes, and the Nature GLP1R-variant finding
pieces.angle: Tirzepatide working less for you than for others? Responses really do differ. Use SURMOUNT-1's spread around the average, with the placebo arm and full population (adults with obesity, or overweight plus at least one weight-related condition, without diabetes, 72 weeks), and SURMOUNT-2's lower average loss in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes, labelled as a separate trial. For the new fact, use the Nature (8 Apr 2026) genetic study of about 28,000 people with self-reported data: a common GLP1R gene variant was linked to slightly more weight loss on both semaglutide and tirzepatide, about 0.76 kg per copy. Frame it as association research that may help explain part of the variation, with no clinical test available and no implication of drug choice. Drop the rare-variant semaglutide-vs-tirzepatide finding, or if kept, cite it correctly as Nature Metabolism, state that tirzepatide response was near-normal in carriers, and never imply switching. Close with 'averages, not predictions' and a question for your prescriber about your own progress, then the don't-switch/stop line, the Exp F line, 'Not personal advice', the prescriber line and the closing line.
pieces.working_title: Tirzepatide Not Working? Why Results Differ #shorts
pieces.why: The Nature paper (13 Nov) adds a fresh tirzepatide-first hook to a high-volume evergreen search. Competition is low, and creators have barely covered it. | fact-check: Source error in the brief. The rare-variant finding ('Rare GLP1R variants attenuate weight loss with semaglutide but not tirzepatide') is in Nature Metabolism (nature.com/articles/s42255-026-01656-z), not 'Nature, Nov 2026'. Search reports put it at about 13,725 treated adults, damaging variants in about 0.2%, and carriers losing roughly a quarter of the usual weight on semaglutide but near-normal amounts on tirzepatide. Its page sits behind a login, so the date and figures need confirming via PubMed or another accessible source. The separate Nature paper (8 Apr 2026, s41586-026-10330-z, 23andMe Research Institute, 27,885 people, self-reported data) found a common GLP1R variant (rs10305420) linked to about 0.76 kg more weight loss per copy on both semaglutide and tirzepatide, and GIPR variants linked to nausea and vomiting on tirzepatide. The rare-variant result can't explain why tirzepatide works less for someone, because tirzepatide response was near-normal in carriers. Using it in a 'tirzepatide not working?' Short implicitly promotes switching drugs and confuses the scope. SURMOUNT-1 and SURMOUNT-2 figures are fine if both arms, populations and the 72-week timeframe are given, and the trials stay labelled as separate.

pieces.topic: Why a greasy or rich meal can hit harder on tirzepatide (slower stomach emptying), and gentler ways to eat it
pieces.angle:
20:00 funnel Short and spin-off of L1, tight arm. It asks one fresh question rather than re-cutting the L1 script.
- Sentence 1: 'Greasy meal hit you harder on tirzepatide? There's a reason.'
- By 6 s, in label wording: tirzepatide delays gastric emptying, and nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea are common. Use one pooled rate per dose vs placebo, matching L1's verified script exactly.
- Advisory line at its exact scope: avoiding fatty or high-fibre foods in the first few days can help ease nausea.
- Untagged tips: a smaller portion, eat slowly, stop at comfortably full, sip fluids unless you've been told to limit them. No 'bad' foods, no guilt, no calorie talk.
- Emergency card: severe stomach pain that won't go away, with or without vomiting, means stop and call your healthcare provider right away. Then the scoped don't-stop line, 'Not personal advice', the prescriber line and the closing line. No Exp F line.
- Post note: the related-video target is L1 once it's verified live, otherwise Side Effects.
pieces.working_title: Tirzepatide and Greasy Food: Why It Hits Harder #shorts
pieces.why: Spin-off of L1, and it drives traffic to the long video. It's a felt symptom in a practical moment, and searches about rich-meal nausea build toward the Nov 20–28 holiday meals.
